genZNote: Lives quietly in everyone's pores until it doesn't — same organism as the acne one you've heard of, formerly filed under Propionibacterium.

morphology.arrangement: Single cells, short chains, or clumps

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human skin, particularly sebaceous (oil) gland-rich areas
habitat.hostAssociation: Major normal microbiota of adult human skin, hair follicles, and pilosebaceous units
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Restricted almost entirely to human skin habitats

culture.media: Anaerobic blood agar; extended incubation (5-14 days) often needed
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, white to cream, convex colonies

identificationClues: Gram-positive pleomorphic 'diphtheroid' rod, easily mistaken for a skin contaminant in blood cultures
Slow growth and extended anaerobic incubation are needed to recover it reliably
Ubiquitous member of normal skin flora — its presence in a specimen doesn't automatically mean infection
Implicated in acne vulgaris pathogenesis and in indolent prosthetic joint/shunt/cardiac device infections

clinicalImportance.transmission: Endogenous — arises from the patient's own skin flora rather than person-to-person spread
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Frequently dismissed as a contaminant in cultures, but a recognized true pathogen in indolent device- and implant-associated infections
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Distinguishing true infection from skin-flora contamination often requires multiple positive cultures or extended incubation

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Normal skin commensal that becomes clinically relevant mainly via implanted devices or acne
